purpose: Hypothesis-only catalog of spreadsheet-work triggers for template research.

visual.title: Print-ready summary block
visual.why: People want the workbook to read cleanly on paper or PDF without reformatting.

visual.title: Large report header with branding
visual.why: The sheet doubles as a document and needs an obvious top-of-page identity area.

visual.title: Fixed totals or KPI sidebar
visual.why: Users need key totals visible while scanning or editing the main table.

visual.title: Table with highlighted exceptions
visual.why: Color and emphasis communicate what needs attention faster than raw values.

visual.title: Calendar-style grid
visual.why: Time-oriented work is easier to manage when days or weeks appear as a visual matrix.

visual.title: Repeated monthly sections
visual.why: Recurring reporting cycles often need each period rendered as a similar block.

visual.title: Progress indicator or completion bar
visual.why: Stakeholders want status at a glance rather than reading every row.

visual.title: Timeline or gantt band
visual.why: Duration planning is easier when tasks sit against a horizontal time axis.

visual.title: Legend or color key
visual.why: Users need a decode step when status colors carry meaning.

visual.title: Summary tiles on a dashboard
visual.why: Decision-makers often start with a compact dashboard before diving into detail.

visual.title: Frozen reference rows or columns
visual.why: The workbook is meant for long scrolling while preserving labels and context.

visual.title: Multi-block form layout
visual.why: Some templates separate identity, line items, notes, and totals into distinct visual zones.

data.title: Append rows into a structured table
data.why: Templates often accumulate repeated entries instead of overwriting prior records.

data.title: Lookup against a master list
data.why: Users reference canonical entities rather than typing names or codes repeatedly.

data.title: Roll up detail rows into a summary
data.why: The sheet has detailed entries but the real value is the aggregated outcome.

data.title: Roll forward the prior period
data.why: Recurring templates inherit structure and formulas from the last cycle.

data.title: Formula cascade across rows or columns
data.why: One computed cell usually needs to propagate to all new records.

data.title: Linked calculations across sheets
data.why: Different tabs often separate raw inputs, working calculations, and outputs.

data.title: Reconcile two source tables
data.why: Users compare imported records with a second list to find gaps or mismatches.

data.title: Track unique IDs or codes
data.why: Templates often need a stable identifier for audit, lookup, or duplication control.

data.title: Status pipeline across stages
data.why: Work items move through a finite lifecycle that needs to be counted or filtered.

data.title: Import into a clean table layout
data.why: External exports need normalization before they can be reused reliably.

data.title: Lookup rates, prices, or coefficients
data.why: A central reference table reduces hard-coded values across many rows.

data.title: Snapshot summary for a reporting date
data.why: A workbook often preserves a point-in-time close rather than only live totals.

validation.title: Required identity fields
validation.why: Key records should not be saved without the person, item, project, or account they belong to.

validation.title: Numeric range constraints
validation.why: Amounts, hours, percentages, and counts need guardrails to avoid invalid entry.

validation.title: Allowed date window
validation.why: Entries should fall inside a reporting period, service window, or active engagement.

validation.title: Fixed status list
validation.why: A closed set of labels keeps workflow counts and filters reliable.

validation.title: Fixed category or class list
validation.why: Categorical inputs need consistency so summaries do not fragment.

validation.title: Cross-field consistency check
validation.why: One field should agree with another, such as dates, totals, or units.

validation.title: Duplicate prevention
validation.why: Repeated records can break totals, approvals, or audit trails.

validation.title: Formula cells should not be edited
validation.why: Calculated fields are easier to trust when users cannot overwrite them directly.

validation.title: Unit normalization
validation.why: Different units need to map to one shared interpretation before calculations.

validation.title: Threshold-based alerts
validation.why: Exceptional values should surface immediately rather than waiting for review.

validation.title: Required note on exception
validation.why: Exceptions often need a human explanation to stay audit-ready.

validation.title: Allowed sequence or dependency order
validation.why: Some fields only make sense if prior steps were completed first.

workflow.title: Draft to submit workflow
workflow.why: A workbook often starts as a working draft and then becomes a reviewed submission.

workflow.title: Review and approval step
workflow.why: Many templates separate entry from sign-off so ownership is explicit.

workflow.title: Backlog to done tracking
workflow.why: Work items move through a queue and the template tracks completion state.

workflow.title: Handoff between owners
workflow.why: Responsibility changes across teams or roles and must stay visible.

workflow.title: Periodic close or lock
workflow.why: A completed cycle becomes read-only so the next cycle can start cleanly.

workflow.title: Recurring check-in or log entry
workflow.why: The same workbook is updated every day, week, or month.

workflow.title: Exception escalation path
workflow.why: Anomalies need a next step rather than just being flagged.

workflow.title: Request to fulfillment flow
workflow.why: One sheet tracks what was asked for, another what was delivered.

workflow.title: Quote to invoice progression
workflow.why: Commercial templates often transform a pre-sales artifact into billing output.

workflow.title: Reconciliation cycle
workflow.why: Users compare sources, resolve differences, and document the final state.

workflow.title: Status review meeting pack
workflow.why: A workbook feeds a recurring review where only the latest status matters.

workflow.title: Audit trail and sign-off
workflow.why: People need to know who changed what and when before the workbook is trusted.

domain.title: Finance close package
domain.why: Closing workbooks combine reconciliations, summaries, and controlled outputs.

domain.title: Sales and billing workspace
domain.why: Commercial teams need line items, terms, taxes, and printable customer-facing forms.

domain.title: Inventory control workbook
domain.why: Stock templates track quantities, movements, thresholds, and reorder decisions.

domain.title: People operations tracker
domain.why: HR-adjacent sheets manage attendance, onboarding, and recurring status updates.

domain.title: Project delivery tracker
domain.why: Delivery sheets merge milestones, owners, dependencies, and timeline views.

domain.title: Maintenance and service log
domain.why: Operational logs capture inspections, incidents, fixes, and closure notes.

domain.title: Health or wellness tracker
domain.why: Personal tracking sheets combine measurements, thresholds, and trends over time.

domain.title: Education roster and grade tracker
domain.why: Classroom templates blend rosters, attendance, and assessment summaries.

domain.title: Procurement cycle tracker
domain.why: Procurement workbooks move from request through approval to receipt and payment.

domain.title: Logistics planning sheet
domain.why: Dispatch and delivery planning need routes, dates, loads, and timing windows.

domain.title: Risk or compliance register
domain.why: Control-oriented sheets track issues, controls, owners, due dates, and exceptions.

domain.title: Asset register
domain.why: Asset records need unique identifiers, lifecycle state, and periodic review.
